root_idea.summary: The supplied evidence centers this root's Quranic lexical field on prayer, supplication, blessing, places of prayer, and those who pray.
root_idea.development: The packet supplies no matched Maqāyīs entry. Lane records additional, distinct branches involving the rear or back, striking, racing, and related derived formations; these are preserved separately rather than collapsed into the Quranic prayer vocabulary.

senses.usage_conditions: Used for the religious act of prayer; grammatical aspect and person vary across the Quranic forms.

senses.definition: To pray or supplicate for someone; to invoke good, forgiveness, or commendation on their behalf.
senses.usage_conditions: Commonly occurs with عَلَى naming the person for whom the prayer is made. The construction may be used of a human or an angelic subject.

senses.definition: To bless, confer blessing, show mercy, or magnify and honor.
senses.usage_conditions: With God as subject, the construction denotes the conferral of blessing, mercy, honor, or magnification; with angels or people, it denotes invoking such blessing, especially in the Quranic expression concerning the Prophet.

senses.definition: Prayer, supplication, or petition, including prayer made on behalf of another.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the broader nominal sense from which more specialized religious uses develop; the Quran also uses it in expressions of prayer or blessing for persons.

senses.definition: The prescribed religious prayer or service.
senses.usage_conditions: A conventional religious act comprising prayer and, in its fully specified form, bowing and prostration; the Quran frequently presents it as an established practice to be performed or maintained.

senses.definition: Blessing, mercy, commendation, or divine favor.
senses.usage_conditions: With God as the source, it denotes blessing, mercy, commendation, or magnification; in human usage it may denote an invocation of blessing. The Quranic plural can refer to blessings from God or to blessings invoked by people.

senses.definition: A place of worship, specifically a synagogue or Jewish house of worship in the Quranic plural expression.
senses.usage_conditions: This sense occurs in the Quranic plural صَلَوَاتٌ within a list of protected houses of worship; it is distinct from the ordinary singular sense “prayer.”
The Quranic occurrence denotes a place set apart for prayer; the form is a place noun derived from the prayer vocabulary.

senses.definition: One who prays; a person performing the prescribed prayer.
senses.usage_conditions: The supplied Quranic occurrences are masculine plural active-participle forms, but the lexical sense is the agent noun “one who prays.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike or beat the صَلًا, the middle or rear part of a person or quadruped, with an object, arrow, or similar implement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal verbal usage; the object is the bodily part called صَلًا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse, to follow immediately after the foremost horse at the finish of a race.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A racing term, explained by reference to the horse's position next to the foremost horse's rear parts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a wild ass, to drive his she-asses together and make them follow the way he takes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological and behavioral usage of the Form II verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a mare or she-camel, to become relaxed around the tail or rump when near parturition; of a she-camel, for the young to fall into the part called صَلًا.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV usage restricted by the lexical evidence to a mare or she-camel in the approach to giving birth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The middle or rear part of the back or rump, including the region beside or supporting the tail and the associated bones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term has several closely related anatomical applications for humans and quadrupeds. The idiom جِئْتُ فِي أَصْلَائِهِمْ means “I came at their rears.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A conventional designation for the Fātiḥah, or Opening Chapter, as a form of prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metonymic conventional use in the expression سُورَةُ الصَّلَاةِ; it is not a separate Quranic form meaning in the supplied QAC occurrences.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have sexual intercourse with a woman anally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare classical construction recorded as a separate nominal branch and not attested among the supplied Quranic usages.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mare or she-camel in the near-parturition state described under أَصْلَتْ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine active participle referring to the animal undergoing that condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A carpet or mat on which the prescribed prayer is performed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete object sense distinct from the place noun used in the Quranic occurrence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The horse that comes immediately after the foremost horse in a race.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A racing noun homonymous with the active participle “one who prays.”
